Reads as coherent two-storey jettied Tudor cottage from every angle, above generic bar

config.style: Tudor half-timbered jettied two-storey cottage: cream plaster + dark timber frame with diagonal braces, pitched slate roof with plaster gable ends, brick side chimney, mullioned glass windows, 5x7 recessed plank door

steps: get_references('tudor half-timbered house') - noted signature features: dark timber grid + diagonal braces on white plaster, jettied upper floor, steep roof, mullioned windows

Assembled Model from primitives via run_luau at (110,110): stone plinth, ground-floor walls with 5w x 7h door opening, jettied upper floor (+1.5 stud overhang), wedge gable ends, two slate roof slabs + ridge cap
Applied timber frame: sills/rails/corner posts/studs/diagonal braces proud of the plaster on front and both sides
Added 3 front + 1 side mullioned glass windows, recessed plank door with knob, brick chimney with stone cap
capture_angles round 1 caught inverted gable wedges (notch at ridge); rebuilt both gable pairs with corrected wedge orientation
capture_angles round 2 (front/right/iso) confirmed coherent silhouette and reference features on every side

recipe.text: Recipe: build the shell as banded boxes (plinth 1, ground 1-10, jetty floor, upper 10-18, ridge 26) with the door as three wall segments (L/R + lintel band) so the opening is real. Jetty = push the upper front wall out 1.5 studs and cover the underside with a plank board. Gables = two wedges per end, thin edges outward, tall edges meeting at center; roof = two rotated slabs (atan2(rise,halfspan)) + ridge cap. Timber frame reads Tudor only if beams sit ~0.2 studs PROUD of the plaster; diagonal braces sell it. Scale check: door 5x7, storeys 8-9 studs vs 5-stud character.
